narrative.overview:
Everything is made of one physical material: a pale mineral ground, deep teal slabs cut to interlock, and frosted panes seated in notches that the slabs leave open. A pane's halo, drawn in the ground colour, is what carves the notch. The system serves two surfaces. The showcase page (Experience mode, judges and demo viewers) is the object at full scale: a wordmark slab, a pinned live phone, panes tucked at asymmetric corners. The phone app (Operate mode, a kirana owner at the counter, one-handed, noisy) borrows the same grammar in finance-app form: a hero card with a notch, round icon buttons, rows with the time under the name, a floating pill nav with a voice circle that rises out of it.

Density is low and numbers are large. The user may not read comfortably, so rupee amounts in condensed teal-black numerals and short labels in the shopkeeper's language carry the screen. Depth is dimensional and soft-lit rather than flat: long, blurred, teal-tinted drop shadows under slabs and cards. Amber is the single attention colour and appears as an object, never as a wash.
keyCharacteristics: One material: ground, slab, pane. Surfaces are cut and nested, not stacked as equal cards.
Condensed Big Shoulders numerals and wordmark against calm Figtree text.
Pills and capsules for every control; large radii on every container.
Credit is amber-brown, payment is green-teal, notes are violet, and each is always paired with an arrow icon and a word.
The phone ships a light and a dark theme; the showcase is light only.
Motion explains state: the voice circle changes with the voice, the chapters crossfade with scroll. Nothing else moves for show.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only chromatic family in the chrome. Amber, brown, green, violet and red appear only as a named object or a money/state meaning, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Word And Arrow Rule
rules.body: Credit and payment are never told apart by colour alone: each carries an arrow icon and its word (udhaar, jama).

rules.name: The Ground Halo Rule
rules.body: A notch is made by a box-shadow ring in the exact ground colour (14px on the showcase, 10px on the phone). The ring colour must match the ground it sits on, in both themes.

rules.name: The Numerals Are Display Rule
rules.body: Every money amount and count uses Big Shoulders with tabular lining figures; running text never does.

rules.name: The Native Script Rule
rules.body: Devanagari and Kannada render in their Noto faces through the font stack; never size or weight-substitute them with a Latin-only face.

rules.name: The Seated Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always offset downward with negative spread and a teal tint, never zero-offset glow and never a hard offset block.

rules.name: The Crossfade Plateau Rule
rules.body: Each chapter is fully sharp for the middle 75% of its scroll span and fully hidden before the next begins; no two chapters are ever readable at once.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: With prefers-reduced-motion, the orb stops all animation and shows a static form for each state; the toast and scroll arrow stop; smooth scrolling is off; chapters still crossfade by opacity without rise or blur.

dos: Do build every new container as a slab, pane or raised card in the existing radii, with the Ground Halo wherever a piece sits in a notch.
Do set every amount in Big Shoulders 800 with tabular lining figures, and keep text in Figtree.
Do pair credit and payment colour with an arrow and a word, and give each state a text label as well as a colour.
Do keep every touch target at 44px or more and primary actions at 56px, and keep text at 13px or more.
Do define colours as variables on :root with a full [data-theme='dark'] override on the phone.
Do keep amber for attention objects only (peek card, demo chip, toast action, thinking state, toggle knob).
donts: Don't use a hard offset shadow, a zero-offset glow or a gradient on text.
Don't stack equal, same-size cards in a row; vary size and corner so slabs and panes interlock.
Don't add another accent hue or use red or violet decoratively.
Don't rely on colour alone, and don't use Big Shoulders for running text or Latin-only fonts for Hindi or Kannada.
Don't add a motion that is not tied to a state or to scroll position, and don't skip the reduced-motion branch for a new animation.
Don't copy the direction contract text into any browser-delivered file.
